business_scope.primary_industry_name: Operating and Financial Leasing of Turbofan Aircraft Engines

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Cook Islands (self-governing state in free association with New Zealand)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English common-law heritage as applied by the High Court and Court of Appeal of the Cook Islands, supplemented by local statutory law and customary-law elements)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: No autonomous Cook Islands bilateral investment treaty, double taxation agreement or free trade agreement is in force. New Zealand's BIT/DTAA/FTA network does not extend to the Cook Islands: standard territorial-application clauses in New Zealand's investment and tax treaties generally exclude the Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau in the absence of express extension.

Free-association and overarching relationship instruments with New Zealand (Joint Centenary Declaration of the Principles of the Relationship between the Cook Islands and New Zealand, 2001) govern citizenship, defence and consular representation; they confer no substantive investment-protection or tax-treaty benefits.

Aviation operating context: Convention on International Civil Aviation (Chicago Convention 1944, ICAO) applies to aircraft registration and lessor/lessee operational certificates; the Cape Town Convention on International Interests in Mobile Equipment 2001 and its Aircraft Protocol are not ratified by the Cook Islands, and engine lessor remedies must therefore be protected contractually through deregistration powers, governing law, insurance assignments and escrow release mechanics.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), principally sections 12 (registration), 14 (constitution), 15 (separate legal entity), 17-19 (incorporation procedure), 20-26 (company name), 30-33 (registered office and address for service), 46-59 (share issues), 128-151 (share capital and distributions), 152-195 (directors, duties, and governance), and the Financial Reporting Act 2013 (financial statement and audit obligations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, an operational business unit within the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the New Zealand Companies Register and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZCO1 / Form 1: Application for Registration of a Company under section 18 of the Companies Act 1993, filed via the online Companies Register portal (https://www.companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a company limited by shares under the Companies Act 1993 (ss 46, 128). Shares may be issued at a price determined by the subscriber or board, including for nominal consideration (e.g., NZD 1 per share); no government escrow or impoundment account is required for share capital. If the lease transaction requires rental security, pre-payment, or debt-service reserves, the parties may contractually establish an escrow account with a licensed NZ bank, but this is a commercial arrangement, not a statutory condition of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FORMAL FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION

COMPANY: [INTERNATIONAL COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (COMPANY NUMBER: [●]; NZBN: [●])
INCORPORATED UNDER THE COMPANIES ACT 1993

UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTIONS OF THE SOLE SUBSCRIBER AND THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS
Adopted on [●] 2025 pursuant to section 122 of the Companies Act 1993, the constitution of the Company, and all applicable law.

WHEREAS:
A. The Company was duly incorporated as a company limited by shares on [●] 2025 in New Zealand, with a constitution whose objects include acquiring, holding, financing, leasing, sub-leasing, and disposing of turbofan aircraft engines and related aviation assets and conducting cross-border aviation asset leasing, including dry leasing of engines to air carriers.
B. The founding subscriber has subscribed for the entire initial share capital of the Company.
C. The directors intend to establish the Company's corporate governance, banking, and leasing mandate consistent with prudent aviation leasing practice and New Zealand law.

NOW IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT
RESOLVED that the subscription and allotment of the initial share capital set out in Schedule A be and hereby are ratified and confirmed, such allotment having been made in accordance with sections 46 to 59 of the Companies Act 1993; that the Company's register of members shall be duly maintained and made open for inspection; and that the directors may in future issue further shares as commercial circumstances require.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE AND ADDRESS FOR SERVICE
RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be and hereby is established and maintained at [full street address, New Zealand], a physical place open to the public, in compliance with section 30 of the Companies Act 1993; and that the address for service of the Company be notified to the Companies Office and kept current forthwith upon any change.

3. APPOINTMENT OF DIRECTORS AND OFFICERS
RESOLVED that [Name 1] (Chairperson), [Name 2], and [Name 3] be and hereby are appointed as the first directors of the Company; that at least one director satisfied the New Zealand residence requirement of section 155(2) of the Companies Act 1993; that [Name 4] be appointed Company Secretary; and that [corporate service provider] be appointed as registered office agent and share registry agent.

4. BANKING, SWIFT WIRE, AND ESCROW AUTHORISATIONS
RESOLVED that the Company's principal banker shall be a licensed registered bank in New Zealand, and that the directors be and hereby are authorised to open, maintain, and operate corporate current accounts, foreign currency accounts, and escrow accounts for aircraft engine lease transactions, noting the Company's target payment rails of SWIFT wire and escrow settlements; and that any two of the Chairperson, Managing Director, and Chief Financial Officer shall be joint authorised signatories.

5. LEASING, FINANCING, AND TRANSACTION AUTHORITY
RESOLVED that the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and any two directors acting jointly are hereby authorised to negotiate, execute, and deliver dry engine lease agreements, financial and operating lease instruments, sale and leaseback agreements, security and collateral assignment documents, escrow collateral instructions, warranty assignments, maintenance and power-by-the-hour service documents, and all ancillary aviation asset instruments with approved air carriers, financiers, and counterparties.

6. STATUTORY FILING AND COMPLIANCE OBLIGATIONS
RESOLVED that the Company Secretary shall procure that all statutory returns, annual returns, beneficial ownership information, financial statements, and notices required under the Companies Act 1993, the Financial Reporting Act 2013, and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 are prepared and filed within statutory deadlines; and that the directors shall cause the Company to maintain a proper compliance and risk register appropriate to an aviation lessor classified as a medium-risk enhanced business.

7. GENERAL RATIFICATION
RESOLVED that all acts, engagements, and expenditures undertaken by the subscriber or any person on behalf of the Company prior to the date of these resolutions be and hereby are ratified and confirmed; and that each director acknowledges and accepts the directors' duties imposed by sections 131 to 137 of the Companies Act 1993.

DATED this [●] day of [●], 2025.

_____________________________
[Director 1] - Chairperson

_____________________________
[Director 2]

_____________________________
[Company Secretary]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal Structure Confirmation and Constitutional Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate counsel, notary public, and New Zealand Companies Office (accreditation of the registered office agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a statutory eligibility review for a company limited by shares under the Companies Act 1993. Confirm the business object of aircraft engine dry leasing is lawful and not reserved. If custom constitutional powers are desired (e.g., granting the board power to enter into engine leasing, acquisition, and security documents), draft and adopt a constitution under section 14. If no constitution is adopted, the default provisions of the Companies Act 1993 apply. Identify at least one natural person director who is a New Zealand resident or licensed under section 155(2). Prepare beneficial ownership information for the Companies Office and the AML/CFT compliance file. Execute the subscriber consent and the pro forma first board resolution.
required_dossiers: Certificate/evidence of identity (passport or national ID) for each director and shareholder
Proof of address for each director and shareholder (utility bill or bank statement no older than 3 months)
Beneficial ownership declaration and corporate ownership chart, including any trust or offshore parent
Proposed constitution (if customized) or written election to rely on the Companies Act 1993 default regime
Consent to Act as Director (Form NZCO4 equivalent)
Draft first board resolution for subscriber and initial directors
AML/CFT due diligence questionnaire completed by the founding shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office or the Registrar queries the object clause, the constitution, or the beneficial ownership declaration, amend the document and re-file; if a director fails the residence requirement, appoint an alternative New Zealand-resident director within the statutory requisition period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register Online Name Reservation Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a name availability check on the Companies Office website using the proposed company name, e.g., '[Name] International Company Limited'. The name must end with 'Limited' unless an exemption under section 21 of the Companies Act 1993 applies. Submit an online name reservation, which secures the name for a limited period (usually 20 working days) and can be renewed. Verify that the name is not misleading, does not connote any prohibited activity, and does not infringe any existing registered trade mark in New Zealand (IPONZ search recommended).
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (primary and up to 3 alternatives)
Online name availability search result
Name reservation application and NominalName fee payment record
If using 'International Company' or 'IC', a short explanatory statement that the company conducts cross-border aircraft engine leasing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or requisitioned by the Registrar, respond in writing with evidence of non-misleading use, or select an alternative available name and reserve it. A refused name decision may be appealed to the High Court of New Zealand under the Companies Act 1993, but the practical cure is substitution of name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Subscriber and Board Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding subscriber, proposed directors, notary public, and corporate secretarial provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a formal board meeting or execute written resolutions. Ratify the allotment of shares to the founding subscriber (including share number, class, and consideration) and adopt the registered office as set out in the first board resolution. Appoint the initial directors, company secretary (if any), and banking signatories. Confirm the governance policy for SWIFT wire and escrow account operations. Ensure each director signs the consent to act form and acknowledges duties under sections 131-137 to act in good faith and in the best interests of the Company.
required_dossiers: Signed first board resolution and subscriber resolution
Consent to act as director (Form NZCO4 equivalent)
Minutes of the incorporation meeting or unanimous written resolutions
Share register opening page
Bank signatory mandate template (for later bank account opening)
Registered office consent letter from the registered office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any director or shareholder refuses to sign, the instrument may be corrected and re-executed; if a board appointment is defective, the defect is cured by a later unanimous resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, online Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit Form 1 (Application for Registration of a Company) through the online Companies Register portal. Provide the company name, registered office address, address for service, full names and birth dates of all directors, particulars of the resident director, share structure, constitution (if adopted), and beneficial ownership disclosures. Attach the consent to act forms and any constitutional documents. Electronically sign the application as subscriber and complete the declaration of compliance. Submit the application and pay the statutory filing fee of NZD 105 (approximately USD 66). The application is reviewed against the Companies Act 1993 and the Registrar's compliance rules.
required_dossiers: Completed Form 1 / NZCO1 application for registration
Consent to act for each director (Form NZCO4)
Memorandum of constitution and signed constitution adoption (if any)
Name reservation certificate or approved name
Registered office consent letter
Proof of identity of the New Zealand-resident director
Beneficial ownership schedule and AML/CFT source-of-funds declaration
Statutory filing fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition under section 19 for incomplete information, the applicant must correct and resubmit within the stated window (usually 20 working days); failure to respond results in rejection, in which case the applicant files a new application and pays the fee afresh.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful review, the Registrar signs and issues an electronic Certificate of Incorporation under section 18(3) of the Companies Act 1993, which conclusively evidences incorporation. The Registrar electronically assigns the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). Verify that the resolution date, company number, NZBN, directors, and registered office are correctly reflected on the public register. Download and archive the certificate, the register extract, and the NZBN record in the Company's statutory minute book. If a constitution was adopted, ensure the constitution is filed and publicly accessible where required by law.
required_dossiers: Electronic Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN registration record
Companies Register current extract
Company number and name reservation confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or register extract contains typographical errors or incomplete information, apply to the Companies Office for an administrative correction under the Companies Act 1993 and the Companies (Documents) Regulations; if the NZBN is incorrect, use the NZBN Change of Details service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations with Inland Revenue (IRD Number, GST, and Non-Resident Status)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand Government
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for an IRD number under the Tax Administration Act 1994 using the appropriate entity application form (company and non-resident company application form IR596 for a company managed and controlled outside New Zealand). If the Company is treated as non-resident for New Zealand tax because its central management and control is outside New Zealand, only New Zealand-source income is taxable in New Zealand. Register for GST under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 if the Company makes GST-registrable supplies in New Zealand; where the dry-lease rentals are supplied to non-resident airlines and the engines remain outside New Zealand, the supplies may be zero-rated or outside the scope of GST. Apply for withholding tax registration and obtain an IRD number for non-resident contractor payments only if applicable. Confirm the 'International Company' profile may be structured to derive only foreign-sourced lease income and maintain a tax-exempt status within the applicable New Zealand tax framework; however, any New Zealand-source income will be subject to income tax or non-resident withholding tax.
required_dossiers: Application for IRD number (Form IR596 for non-resident company)
Certificate of Incorporation
Registered Office and Director details (asset approval letter from Companies Office)
Constitution and board resolution regarding tax residency and foreign-source income
Ownership and beneficial ownership chart of the ultimate shareholder
Estimated revenue profile and description of the engine lease transactions
GST registration application (if required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD queries the non-resident or foreign-sourced income status, respond with a legal opinion from an accredited New Zealand tax counsel and supporting board minutes evidencing that central management and control is exercised outside New Zealand; if the IRD issues an assessment contrary to the taxpayer's position, the taxpayer may file a notice of proposed adjustment (NOPA) and escalate through the disputes procedure under Part 4A of the Tax Administration Act 1994.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Financial Service Provider, AML/CFT, and Civil Aviation Regulatory Assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR), and Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand (CAA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assess whether the aircraft engine dry-leasing business constitutes 'financial services' under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008; for a pure operating dry lease to a commercial airline, FSPR registration is generally not required, but where financing elements, credit, or lending are present, register on the FSPR and join an approved dispute resolution scheme. Perform an AML/CFT risk assessment under section 18 of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, classifying the aviation leasing business as 'Medium-Risk Enhanced' and adopt an enhanced customer due diligence programme for counterparties and beneficial owners. With the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand, confirm that the Company does not hold an Air Operator Certificate because it does not operate aircraft; since engine airworthiness is maintained by the lessee, fewer than CAA Part 119/125/129 obligations apply; confirm any record-keeping requirements for commercial transport engine transactions.
required_dossiers: Legal memorandum on FSP Act and AML/CFT Act application to engine leasing
AML/CFT risk assessment and compliance programme
Customer due diligence policy and enhanced due diligence templates
Counterparty profile for air carrier lessees
Copy of the engine lease and escrow structure description
CAA determination or clarification letter regarding no Air Operator Certificate requirement
FSPR Notice of Registration (if mandatory)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FMA queries FSPR status, file an amending notice or withdraw the application if not required; if the CAA determines that the Company is an aircraft/engine operator because it retains operational control, then apply for the appropriate civil aviation certification or restructure the lease so that operational control passes to the lessee; AML/CFT deficiencies are cured by adopting an enhanced compliance programme and training record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account, SWIFT Wire, and Escrow Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed New Zealand registered bank (authorised under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021) and corporate banking relationship team
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the certified corporate document package to the bank and open the Company's primary operating account, a dedicated escrow/collection account for lease rentals, and any foreign currency settlement sub-accounts. Complete the bank's account opening forms, including transaction profiling for high-value international engine leasing payments via SWIFT wire. Provide beneficial ownership identification, source of funds and wealth statements, and a certified copy of the board resolution authorising signatories and SWIFT/escrow operation. Establish dual-signatory controls for disbursement above USD 25,000; execute the bank's Master Escrow Agreement for the collection of lease rentals and security deposits. Activate the account once the bank's AML/CFT onboarding committee gives clearance.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN record
Constitution and first board resolution (banking mandate pages)
Passport-quality identity documents for all directors and beneficial owners
Proof of residential address for each signatory
Company tax registration record (IRD number confirmation)
Bank account opening and SWIFT wire mandate forms
Escrow account service agreement
AML/CFT due diligence questionnaire and source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence documents, provide the beneficial ownership chart and lease counterparty list; if the application is declined on AML/CFT grounds, remediate the compliance framework and apply to another licensed bank or a locally incorporated branch; this is a commercial decision and not a statutory incorporation remedy.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand (CAA); no industrial manufacturing authority applies because the Company is an aircraft engine lessor and does not operate an overhaul shop or manufacturing facility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Nil for pure dry-leasing: no Air Operator Certificate (CAA Part 119/125/129), no Aviation Maintenance Organisation Certificate (CAA Part 145), and no airworthiness certificate is held by the lessor in its own capacity; the lessee/operator is responsible for engine airworthiness compliance under Civil Aviation Rules Part 43. Should the Company later establish an engine storage, teardown, or part-out facility, a building consent and resource consent from the territorial authority would be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, acting under the Environmental Protection Authority Act 2011, in coordination with the territorial regional council under the Resource Management Act 1991 (RMA 1991); for a head-office and leasing-only activity, the lead consent authority is the relevant city/district council.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category 3 (Administrative record only). No formal Environmental Impact Assessment Report is required because the business activity is an office-based, asset-leasing operation with no discharge of contaminants to air, land, or water, no hazardous substance handling, and no industrial and trade activities listed in Schedule 1 of the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Air Quality) Regulations 2004 or Schedule 4 of the RMA 1991. The activity emits no measurable environmental pollution.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for the leasing-only stage. The Company will maintain administrative compliance with the RMA 1991 s 17 duty to avoid unreasonable noise, and with office waste disposal obligations under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008. If future premises include an engine storage or maintenance annex, then the following thresholds would apply: stormwater and wastewater must meet the National Environmental Standard enforceable by the regional council under RMA 1991; VOC emissions threshold of 0.4 kg per hour or 72 tonnes per annum under the National Air Quality Standards would be the applicable ceiling before a discharge permit is required; electrical and hazardous waste must be handled by an EPA-registered waste contractor.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate and Building Code compliance: the registered office and any ancillary premises must hold an annual Fire Safety Certificate for means of escape, alarms, and extinguishing systems issued under the Building Act 2004 (clauses 3.11-3.13, Building Code) and certified by accredited fire safety engineers. Structural load inspection is not required for ordinary occupancy of a leased office, but any hangar or engine storage structure must have a structural engineer's certificate and a building warrant of fitness. Occupational clearance: the office must comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015; the Company must implement a general risk and workplace management programme under the Health and Safety at Work (General Risk and Workplace Management) Regulations 2016, including hazard registers, first aid, and emergency evacuation plans. No hazardous industrial licence is required for a pure head-office lessor.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue (Inland Revenue Department / Te Tari Taake), Wellington, New Zealand; taxpayer portal: myIR at https://www.ird.govt.nz; customs and export documentation are administered separately by the New Zealand Customs Service (Trade Single Window / SWIFT)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) is a non-resident foreign company for New Zealand tax purposes and is not required to obtain an IRD number unless it derives New Zealand-sourced income, has a fixed establishment in New Zealand, or voluntarily registers for GST to claim input credits or to zero-rate cross-border supplies. Procedure: (1) File Form IR742 'Application for IRD Number for a Non-Resident Company' with Inland Revenue; (2) attach certified copies of the Cook Islands Certificate of Incorporation, the constitution/articles of association, the register of directors, the ultimate beneficial ownership declarations under the AML/CFT rules, and the aircraft engine dry lease agreement; (3) simultaneously submit a GST registration application (Form GST1) if net annual taxable turnover exceeds NZD 60,000 or if voluntary registration is sought; (4) upon approval, Inland Revenue issues an 8-9 digit IRD number by letter confirming the registration; (5) a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) may be obtained separately from the Companies Office only if the IC establishes a place of business or registers a branch in New Zealand. Any physical import/export of aircraft engines requires a Customs client code (CC code) from the New Zealand Customs Service in addition to the IRD number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope (with the Cook Islands IC noted as a Tax_Exempt_Zone entity in its domestic jurisdiction; however, under the Income Tax Act 2007 the CK_IC is treated as a non-resident entity-level taxpayer subject to New Zealand income tax only on New Zealand-sourced income. It is not eligible for pass-through or look-through company treatment in New Zealand; foreign-sourced lease income from engines located wholly outside New Zealand is not subject to New Zealand tax unless derived through a fixed establishment in New Zealand. Dividends, interest, and certain royalties sourced from New Zealand remain subject to non-resident withholding tax where applicable)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no 'check-the-box' or equivalent entity classification election; entity status is statutory and non-elective. Available elections relevant to a non-resident aviation lessor include: (1) voluntary registration for GST (Section 51 GST Act 1985) to enable zero-rating of export supplies, notwithstanding that the lessor is non-resident; (2) GST group registration election under Section 55 of the GST Act 1985 if a fixed establishment and closely-related entities exist in New Zealand; (3) election to be treated as having a taxable activity in New Zealand solely for the purpose of the reverse charge rules on imported services; (4) for NZ-resident counterparties, hybrid mismatch rules under Part FM of the Income Tax Act 2007 apply and cannot be elected away; the CK_IC should obtain a binding product ruling from Inland Revenue in respect of the zero-rating of engine leases and the absence of a New Zealand permanent establishment

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 (annual turnover from taxable supplies made in New Zealand over any 12-month period); NZD 130,000 for non-profit bodies; non-resident suppliers of 'remote services' or intangibles are subject to the same NZD 60,000 threshold on their New Zealand-resident customers; for the CK_IC, cross-border dry leases of aircraft engines located outside New Zealand are generally outside the threshold because the supply is zero-rated export supply, but voluntary registration is commonly adopted to maintain clean invoicing and refund of GST on any New Zealand-sourced expenses (e.g., storage, insurance, legal)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no API e-invoicing clearance, and no digital stamping regime exists in New Zealand. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates through the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 network (National e-Invoicing Solution); in any event, a valid GST tax invoice must contain: the words 'Tax Invoice', the supplier's name, address and GST number, the recipient's name, a sequential invoice number, invoice date, description and quantity of the supply, consideration, and the GST content. For zero-rated export supplies, the invoice must be endorsed with the statement 'Zero-Rated (0% GST)' and the underlying export evidence retained. New Zealand Customs Service operates a real-time export declaration platform (Trade Single Window) for physical exports, separate from GST filing via myIR.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Section 11(1)(b) of the GST Act 1985, services (including a dry lease of an aircraft engine) are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, provided the services are not supplied directly in connection with land in New Zealand, not physically performed in New Zealand in circumstances where the recipient is in New Zealand, and not domestic transport or telecommunications services; additionally, Section 11(1)(a) zero-rates exported goods where the engine is physically removed from New Zealand within 28 days of supply. For the CK_IC structure, the dry lease is zero-rated when: (i) the lessee is a non-resident airline or operator with no fixed establishment in New Zealand; (ii) the engine is physically located and operated wholly outside New Zealand during the lease term; (iii) the contract is a true dry lease (no crew, no operating services performed in New Zealand); and (iv) the lessors' New Zealand presence does not constitute a fixed establishment. If the engine is ever imported temporarily into New Zealand for heavy maintenance or storage, the zero-rating may be lost and import GST charged, unless the temporary import bond regime applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Export Entry (Export Declaration) filed through the Trade Single Window / SWIFT portal, where the engine physically departs New Zealand
Original or certified clean Bill of Lading / Master Air Waybill evidencing consignment of the aircraft engine to a foreign lessee outside New Zealand
Commercial Invoice / GST Tax Invoice annotated 'Zero-Rated (0% GST)' and bearing the CK_IC's New Zealand GST registration number
Aircraft Engine Dry Lease Agreement certifying the engine serial number, lessee's offshore address, lease term, and covenant that the engine will not be operated in New Zealand airspace
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by a registered New Zealand bank evidencing receipt of lease rental proceeds in foreign currency from an overseas payer
Engine handover and redelivery certificates, maintenance logbooks, and GPS tracking reports demonstrating continuous physical location of the engine outside New Zealand
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The zero-rating of aircraft engine lease income is subject to audit scrutiny by Inland Revenue and the New Zealand Customs Service. If the CK_IC cannot substantiate the offshore location of the engine and the non-resident status of the lessee, Inland Revenue may assess GST at 15% on the full lease consideration, effectively clawing back the zero-rating with retrospective effect. Penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 include: shortfall penalties for not taking reasonable care (20% of the GST shortfall), unacceptable tax positions (20% or 40%), abusive tax positions (100%), evasion (150%), and goods and services tax evasion criminal prosecutions; use-of-money interest accrues on unpaid GST from the date the return was due. Additionally, if an engine that was exported under Section 11(1)(a) is subsequently re-imported to New Zealand for domestic use without an exemption, import GST becomes payable at the border under Section 12(2) of the GST Act 1985. For false or fraudulent export documentation, the Export (Customs) Rules and Crimes Act 1961 expose the directors and the CK_IC to fines up to NZD 50,000 per offence plus imprisonment; Inland Revenue also retains the power to cancel GST registration and deny refunds where the leasing activity lacks economic substance in New Zealand.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand / Te Pūtea Matua
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully liberalised foreign exchange regime for both current and capital account transactions. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely convertible, and there are no general exchange control laws restricting the transfer of funds into or out of New Zealand, nor any requirement for prior central bank approval for cross-border payments related to aircraft engine dry-leasing or associated trade settlements. Profit remittances are permitted to non-residents, subject to applicable non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) and, where applicable, approved issuer levy (AIL), but no fungibility restriction applies to the underlying conversion or transfer. The exchange control framework is consistent with the IMF's Article VIII obligations; New Zealand accepts convertibility obligations for current international transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory timelines, mandatory conversion ratios, or surrender obligations for export receipts under New Zealand law. Export proceeds derived from dry-leasing income, including lease rentals and related fees invoiced in foreign currencies, may be retained in any designated foreign-currency account or converted to NZD at the exporter's discretion. The absence of export surrender rules also applies to lease payments routed to a New Zealand corporate account from an offshore trustee or lessee, provided the funds are of legitimate origin and comply with the AML/CFT Act 2009 and sanction-screening obligations of the receiving bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with strict limitations. New Zealand does not operate a general Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing regime akin to the EU's EMD2. Non-bank fintech providers wishing to hold or transmit client funds must either be incorporated as registered banks under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 and Banking Prudential Supervision Act 1989, or operate under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 without acquiring a full banking licence. In practice, NZ-registered non-bank payment providers are limited to payment facilitation and cannot offer safeguarded EMI accounts for commercial treasury clients without a bank partner. Offshore digital EMIs may be used as auxiliary payment corridors provided they have valid AML/CFT registrations in their home jurisdictions and enter into back-to-back arrangement with a New Zealand registered bank; however, most domestic tier-1 banks will not treat offshore EMI balances as qualifying operational liquidity for the aircraft engine leasing business. The New Zealand bank account remains the mandatory primary treasury rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: As of the current legal framework, New Zealand banks do not impose a general statutory requirement for directors to appear physically at a branch for corporate account opening, provided that robust remote electronic identity verification (e-ID) satisfies the customer due diligence and AML/CFT obligations under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act). In practice, each covered entity adopts a risk-based approach; for a non-resident International Company with a Cook Islands trustee nexus and aviation-leasing assets, the bank's compliance team will normally require a video-conference interview with at least the beneficial owners and a designated director, coupled with notarised corporate documents and a banker's draft from a recognised trust company. If any beneficial owner appears on enhanced sanctions or PEP screening, or if the source-of-funds explanation is inconsistent, a physical interview at a designated ANZ/ASB/BNZ/Westpac corporate banking branch may be demanded. For the highest onboarding certainty, the directors should be prepared for a remote virtual interview with live verification, but a physical appearance mandate may be imposed on a case-by-case basis for high-risk offshore structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident International Company with Cook Islands trust ownership and no economic substance in New Zealand
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current trust deed or instrument of protection; registered agent certificate from the Cook Islands trust company; certificate of good standing for the International Company; trust asset register evidencing economic substance in respect of the aircraft engine leasing business; bank reference letters from prior relationship banks; and a written economic-substance attestation demonstrating that all leasing contracts, risk management, and treasury functions are managed in New Zealand and are subject to full board oversight.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large-value inbound capital injection for engine acquisition or refinancing exceeding the counterparty's stated net worth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed aircraft engine purchase agreement; dry-lease agreement with the lessee; independent appraiser's valuation of the engine portfolio; source-of-funds file for each material inbound wire, including audited financial statements of the ultimate originator, tax clearance certificates, signed statutory declarations from the remitting entity, and a detailed reconciliation between contractual lease obligations and the capital injection amount.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial ownership chain involving a foreign trustee, discretionary beneficiaries, and layered holding vehicles
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organisational and ownership chart identifying ultimate beneficial owners, trustees, protectors, and any nominee shareholders; authenticated copies of passports for all natural-person beneficiaries with a defined interest; letter of consent from the Cook Islands trust company disclosing the trust details to the New Zealand bank; AML/CFT compliance manual from the trustee; and confirmations that no beneficiary is a politically exposed person or subject to sanctions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border lease payments flowing through multiple jurisdictions with no clear invoice trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Consecutive original invoices issued for each dry-lease rental instalment; lessee's payment instruction and settlement advice; full SWIFT MT103 records for all prior lease payments; engine utilisation and maintenance logs corroborating the lease transaction; correspondence with the lessee's own compliance team; and a certificate from the external auditor confirming the commercial authenticity of the leasing transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential classification as a high-risk medium enhanced scrutiny customer due to ISIC 5223 aircraft engine leasing with low physical assets in New Zealand
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution appointing a New Zealand-based AML/CFT compliance officer; outsourced service level agreement with a New Zealand-approved compliance provider; transactional monitoring programme; independent audit opinion on the effectiveness of the company's anti-money laundering procedures; and a documented risk mitigation matrix specifically addressing turbo-fan engine dry-leasing exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of capital escrow account with a trust company or third-party escrow agent that has no direct banking relationship
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Escrow agreement executed under New Zealand law; regulatory registration certificate of the escrow agent in its home jurisdiction; KYC and KYCC documentation for the escrow agent; flow-of-funds undertaking from the escrow agent confirming that funds are segregated and non-interest-bearing; and a legal opinion from a New Zealand law firm opining that the escrow arrangement does not constitute unauthorised deposit-taking business under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed via SWIFT wire (MT103) to the New Zealand corporate operating account or a dedicated capital escrow account designated for the aircraft engine acquisition. Compliant protocol: (1) instruct the remitting bank to include a clear purpose of payment code relevant to the transaction; for payment of engine lease consideration or financing purposes New Zealand banks generally accept the generic code 'INVCAP' or the ISO 20022 structured category 'Investment Capital'; for trade-related capital injection the remitter should use a purpose narrative stating 'inbound capital injection for acquisition of aircraft engine for operational dry-lease', 'equity contribution', or 'shareholder subordinated loan', as applicable. (2) The remitting bank must include the beneficiary's account number, SWIFT/BIC of the New Zealand bank, and the full legal name and address of the International Company; a remittance slip should be delivered electronically to the receiving relationship manager. (3) The NZ bank may request the underlying loan or equity documentation, a certified beneficiary ownership chart, and confirmation that the transaction is not subject to the Overseas Investment Act 2005 when the asset is not 'sensitive land' or a 'significant business asset' exceeding applicable thresholds; for aircraft engine dry-leasing with no New Zealand land interest and a leasehold value below the statutory threshold, a general legal certificate or self-certification is sufficient. (4) The bank will screen the inbound sender against sanctions lists and verify that the source-of-funds file matches the wire amount and stated purpose; any discrepancy triggers a hold. (5) Once cleared, the funds will be credited in the original foreign currency or converted to NZD at market rate. For the capital escrow account, a written escrow instruction must be provided to the bank contemporaneously with the wire, and the escrow agent must issue a receipt confirming segregation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for the dry-leasing business, including engine acquisition consideration, maintenance reserves, insurance premium payments, and lessor-management fees, may be executed through: (I) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for non-documentary transactions such as periodic rental payments to the lessor, spares purchases, and third-party service fees; each MT103 must include the invoice reference, reason for payment, and where required by the destination jurisdiction a certified commercial invoice in support. (II) Commercial documentary letters of credit (L/C), generally irrevocable at sight, for large transaction-specific disbursements such as purchase of spare engines or major MRO services; the L/C must be advised through a New Zealand bank and confirmed by a prime bank in the beneficiary's jurisdiction when required. (III) Escrow account disbursements under a tripartite escrow agreement; the account bank will release funds only upon joint written instruction by the escrow beneficiary and the escrow agent, or pursuant to a payment certificate certified by an independent engineer for stage completions. (IV) For recurring operational disbursements in the same currency, the company may maintain foreign-currency sub-accounts in USD, EUR, and GBP to avoid unnecessary FX conversion; otherwise conversion is executed at the bank's agreed forward or spot rate with full audit trail. All outbound payments must comply with the bank's transaction monitoring policy, the AML/CFT Act 2009, and the New Zealand financial sanctions requirements; no separate exchange-control approval is required for outbound trade-related payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards (deliverable, NZD vs USD/EUR/GBP) with a registered New Zealand bank

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible under New Zealand law on a standalone OTC basis for sophisticated counterparties, but are not necessary because the NZD is fully deliverable; counterparties should expect higher documentation and collateral requirements under the Financial Market Infrastructures and NZ swap dealer rules.
Interest rate swaps where applicable to hedge floating-rate exposures on engine acquisition debt, provided the company qualifies as an eligible wholesale investor

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the company's annual return date, being the anniversary of incorporation; may be aligned to the balance date with Registrar approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZ$100 (≈US$61); director offence under s. 222 carrying a fine up to NZ$10,000; failure to remedy a Registrar default notice within 20 working days triggers company strike-off (removal) from the New Zealand Register under s. 318.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Income Tax Return (IR4) and Provisional Tax Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date: file by 7 July following year-end; for a non-standard balance date: within six months of the balance date; provisional tax instalments for a standard balance date fall due on 28 August, 15 January, and 7 May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZ$250, with an additional NZ$250 charged every six months of continued non-filing; use-of-money interest and late payment penalties (1% per month) accrue on unpaid tax; IRD may issue an assessment and enforce recovery through collection action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements Filing (financial reporting year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a large or non-exempt company, financial statements must be signed and issued within six months of the balance date and filed with the Registrar within 20 working days after the directors sign and the auditor's report is attached (for a 31 March balance date, no later than late October).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; the company and each director are liable to a fine not exceeding NZ$10,000; repeated default may trigger director disqualification under s. 383 of the Companies Act 1993.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO / Significant Individuals Register Confirmation and Membership Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (transmitted with the Annual Return; maintained for inspection by the Registrar and law enforcement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before each annual return date; interim updates must be recorded in writing within 10 working days of any share transfer or UBO change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Record-keeping offence under the Companies Act 1993 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; civil penalties up to NZ$2,000,000 for reporting entities; directors individually liable for false or suppressed entries.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 applies when the company qualifies as 'large': total assets exceed NZ$60,000,000 (≈US$36,600,000), total annual revenue exceeds NZ$30,000,000 (≈US$18,300,000), or 50 or more full-time employees are engaged (any one test satisfied). A 'small' company (assets ≤ NZ$3m, revenue ≤ NZ$6m, ≤ 12 employees) is exempt from audit but must prepare financial statements. An aircraft engine dry-leasing company with a turbofan engine portfolio exceeding the asset threshold will be 'large' and must obtain a full audit conducted under New Zealand International Standards on Auditing (NZ ISAs).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP) based on IFRS; Tier 1 uses NZ IFRS; Tier 2 uses NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR); small private companies may apply the Simplified Financial Reporting Standard. Lease accounting under NZ IFRS 16 must be applied for aircraft engine operating and finance leases.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Annual Return serves as the annual confirmation of the register of members; any transfer of shares in the engine leasing entity is registered within 10 working days of lodgement of the instrument of transfer under s. 91 of the Companies Act 1993. The company must maintain a Significant Individuals (UBO) register identifying any individual holding or controlling 25% or more of shares or voting rights; the register is confirmed across each annual return cycle and produced to the Registrar or law enforcement on request. The information must be current as at the annual return date, and the company secretary or director must report any material change without undue delay.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (shareholders' resolutions and board minutes)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday or tax-exempt zone exists for an 'International Company' under New Zealand domestic law; a New Zealand-incorporated company is fully tax-resident and taxable on worldwide income at 28%. Effective rate relief arises only from ordinary deductions: IRD economic depreciation for turbofan aircraft engines (general aviation rate category, approximately 24% diminishing value / 17.5% straight-line), finance costs (subject to thin-capitalisation), foreign tax credits under ss LJ-LB, and any available imputation credits. R&D tax incentive (15%) is generally not applicable to a leasing vehicle.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory time bar; New Zealand Income Tax Act 2007 ss IA 4-IA 5). Utilisation of losses is subject to the 49% shareholder continuity rule for the period spanning the loss year and the deduction year, or the business continuity test where ownership changes exceed 49%.
